identity.title: Gemini Planet Imager Observations of the AU Microscopii Debris Disk: Asymmetries within One Arcsecond

paper_type_evidence.quote: we compare our observations with 1.3-mm continuum data from ALMA (cite: macgregor13) and optical imaging using the using the Space Telescope Imaging Spectrograph (STIS)

evidence.quote: At a distance of 9.9 pc, we are able to probe closer to the star than most systems.

question.value: What is the morphology of the AU Mic debris disk within 1 arcsec, and are there planets or compact clumps, as seen with GPI?

evidence.quote: We use GPI in both spectral and polarimetry modes to study the morphology of the debris disk and search for planets close in to the star.

provided.value: K1-band spectral mode and H-band polarimetry mode observations (primary data)

evidence.quote: On 2014 May 12, twenty-seven 60 s spectral mode frames were taken in the K1 spectral band (1.90–2.19 $\mu$m)
optical imaging using the using the Space Telescope Imaging Spectrograph (STIS) on the Hubble Space Telescope (cite: schneider14)

provided.value: Planet detection limits at large separations

evidence.quote: we also included the limits from the Near-Infrared Coronagraphic Imager (cite: wahhaj13) in Figure

what.value: ALMA 1.3-mm continuum reduced data of AU Mic, used for comparison and disk position angle

evidence.quote: we compare our observations with 1.3-mm continuum data from ALMA (cite: macgregor13)

what.value: Disk PA of 128.41 deg derived from ALMA

evidence.quote: using a disk position angle (PA) of $128.41\ensuremath{^\circ}$ (cite: macgregor13) derived from observations with Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA)
We thank M. MacGregor and G. Schneider for making available to us the reduced ALMA and STIS data respectively.
The reduction of the polarimetry mode data follows the steps described in (cite: perrin15_pol).

what.value: Disk model parameters from porous water-ice model

evidence.quote: We adopted values from the porous water-ice model from (cite: graham07)

unstated_but_needed: ALMA data were not reprocessed; the reduced ALMA images came from MacGregor via private communication

method.value: KLIP with ADI (and SDI for spectral mode), annuli and azimuthal sectors

evidence.quote: we used `pyKLIP` (cite: wang15), a Python implementation of the Karhunen-Loève Image Projection (KLIP) algorithm

key_parameters.value: H-band: 3 KL modes with 10-pixel exclusion (left side), 4 KL modes with 6-pixel exclusion (right side)

evidence.quote: we used three KL modes and a ten-pixel exclusion for the diffuse left side of the disk

method.value: Gaussian vertical profile fits between 0.4 and 1.25 arcsec to measure mid-plane offset, FWHM, peak and integrated flux

evidence.quote: fit Gaussian vertical profiles to the disk at various separations. We fit between 0.4$''$ and 1.25$''$.

validation.value: Injected model disks at five positions to correct self-subtraction bias; scatter gives the uncertainties

evidence.quote: The scatter of all four quantities in the model disks were used as the uncertainties in our measurements.

method.value: Contrast curve via Mawet et al. 2014, planet injection, Monte-Carlo completeness with COND models

evidence.quote: we ran a Monte-Carlo analysis as described by (cite: nielsen) to determine the completeness of our data.
assuming COND models (cite: baraffe03)
we used `pyKLIP` (cite: wang15)

used_for.value: Creating datacubes and measuring satellite spots

evidence.quote: a datacube created by the GPI Data Reduction Pipeline (cite: perrin14_drp)

results_numeric.quantity: SE vertical mid-plane offset at 1 arcsec

evidence.quote: an offset from the average ALMA mid-plane of 69$\pm$30 mas to the northeast at 1$''$ separation
with an offset of 47$\pm$8 mas to the southwest at 1$''$
triples on the SE side past 0.8$''$ to a peak FWHM of 570$\pm$56 mas
at a separation of 544$\pm$4 mas, a PA of $130.2\ensuremath{^\circ}$$\pm$$0.9\ensuremath{^\circ}$
a *K1* contrast of 1.1$\pm$0.3 $\times 10^{-5}$

findings_qualitative.value: No polarized signal detected; disk detected only in total intensity

evidence.quote: We did not detect any polarized signal (5% upper limit on the polarization fraction at 0.5$''$)

claims.hypothesis: Is the inner AU Mic disk asymmetric?
claims.experiment: Gaussian vertical profile fits to KLIP-reduced H-band images
claims.result: SE side has a bump at 1 arcsec, three times more extended and fainter in peak brightness, offset 69 mas
claims.finding: Stark SE/NW asymmetries, possibly a warp or the disk backside, agreeing with STIS and ALMA

evidence.quote: The southeast side of the disk exhibits a bump at 1$''$ (10 AU projected separation) that is three times more vertically extended

claims.hypothesis: Are planets present in the inner disk?
claims.experiment: K1 spectral-mode contrast and completeness analysis
claims.result: 50% complete for 4 MJup at 4 AU; one compact candidate at 544 mas
claims.finding: The candidate is either a planet or a disk clump, since it is resolved along the disk

evidence.quote: We detect a source, resolved only along the disk plane, that could either be a candidate planetary mass companion or a compact clump in the disk.

limitations_admitted.value: Disk brightness vs separation unreliable owing to residual PSF features; sliver at only 3.1 sigma and may arise from KLIP self-subtraction

evidence.quote: We cannot rule out that the apparent morphology is influenced by KLIP self-subtraction.

referee_caveats_inferred: Single-epoch GPI data; the candidate is not confirmed by common proper motion
ALMA is used only as comparison, with no reanalysis

missing_for_reproduction: Exact pyKLIP settings beyond KL modes and exclusion
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: not applicable for ALMA; GPI data are a few GB
reproducibility.score_reason: ALMA plays only a comparison role and the main analysis uses GPI data
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: The main data are GPI, not ALMA, and the ALMA data are only a supporting comparison
